title: Benchmark v2 verdict: forced graph usage cost 1.7× for NO correctness gain (graph-dependent, opus, n=5)
summary: v2 forced the ON arm to call get_learnings (mandatory consult) on a task anchored to the real token-a>token-b verdict. Results (n=5, opus, all 10 solved, 0 contamination): OFF gross/net = 325,550±36,792 tok; ON gross = 555,825±124,588, net = 101,710±18,164, plumbing = 454,115±111,665. Headline: gross ON/OFF = 1.71× (ON cost ~70% MORE total); net ON/OFF = 0.31×; wall ON 75.6s vs OFF 62.5s. TWO honest findings: (1) NO correctness/quality benefit — both arms solved 5/5 and the hypothesized 'OFF chases the losing token-b approach' DID NOT happen: OFF transcripts had ZERO claim_session/CLAUDE_SESSION_ID refs and went straight to the winning time-window-overlap approach, because the spec described the algorithm clearly enough that blind agents didn't need the graph. (2) Consulting the graph is EXPENSIVE — ~82% of ON's gross was orchestrator-graph-attributed (get_learnings + large payloads re-read across turns); payload size is the optimization lever. CAVEAT: the net split (0.31×) is NOT fully trustworthy — attribution lumps cache_read of large tool payloads into the plumbing bucket, so net/plumbing absolute numbers have artifacts; the robust top-line is gross 1.7×. COMBINED v1+v2 conclusion: neither a self-contained task (v1: tools sat unused, ~neutral overhead within noise) nor a clear-but-self-solvable task (v2: forced consult, +70% gross, no benefit) made the orchestrator pay off — because in both the graph's knowledge was NOT actually necessary. The orchestrator earns its token cost only when the graph holds knowledge the agent genuinely CANNOT derive alone (preventing real dead-ends/rework) — a scenario neither bench spec successfully created. Next: a genuinely UNDERSPECIFIED task where OFF measurably fails/reworks without the graph.
